negative_reviews.author: Niamh Magee
negative_reviews.text:
Hugely disappointed by this place. It's got great reviews from friends, but I cannot see for the life of me why that would be. The food is extraordinarily bland - I went with a friend who got their spiciest dish and it had no spice to it whatsoever. I got the chicken ramen, and when it first arrived, the chicken was raw. The server explained that the pink colour I was noticing was because it was marinated in pink gin before it was cooked, but that they'd be happy to replace it. My second serving had the same issue. While it wasn't pink, it had the texture of severely undercooked chicken and was translucent in some areas (I've attached a photo, though it was more visible in person). Another server explained that this was due to it being chicken thigh, which makes it more "succulent". I've eaten a lot of chicken thigh in my life and it has never had that texture when cooked. Safe to say I didn't eat anything further.

Every time a customer is seated, a staff member bangs a drum. This is weird, but amusing at first, but quickly becomes incredibly grating. The whole place is decorated like an overdone gimmick of Japan, making it feel more like a cheap Disney display than a comfortable place to eat. I was also disappointed to learn that the £5 ramen offer you get for downloading their app does not apply in this location for whatever reason.

The staff were an absolute delight, and did not charge me for my disastrous meal. They are attentive and friendly, and I can only assume the failures of this place are due to it being a poorly managed chain.

issues: Covers rose to 3,497, up 173 (5.20%) week on week and up 617 (21.42%) year on year.
Spend per head fell to £20.79, down £0.40 (1.89%) week on week and down £1.93 (8.49%) year on year, missing the £22 SPH target.
Without the revenue lost through discounts, spend per head would have been £21.65, and this was the second highest £5 ramen discount value since the app launched.
Sales were £72,694.25, up £2,249.65 (3.19%) week on week and up £7,259.58 (11.09%) year on year, the strongest in the group.
Sales beat the £62,000 target by £10,694.25 (17.24%).
Drinks hit target but sushi and sides did not, against targets of 10%, 20% and 13.5%.

Steak Tataki Ramen (494, plus 67 halal), Chicken Ramen (365) and Black Garlic Tonkotsu (296) were the top sellers, while sea bream nigiri, steak nigiri and surf clam sashimi sold once each and scallop and grilled scallop nigiri twice.
More hours were used than the week before but the wage target was hit, with labour at 19.86% and a FOH and BOH split of 44.85% and 55.15% against a 45% and 55% target.
Food cost was 24.69%, which the BOH meeting flagged as running high.
Food usage variance was 2.8% and wet usage variance 1.1%, both within the acceptable range.
The site received nineteen 5 star, three 4 star, one 3 star and one 2 star Google reviews.
The 2 star review on 01/10 found the food bland, with the chicken ramen broth light and the chicken looking raw; FOH explained and Yan Ha confirmed the team follows the recipe.
A customer also commented on the drum hitting greeting.
Weekly hygiene compliance scored 100% against a 95% target, and pest control, fire, electrical, gas and ventilation compliance are complete.
Rory's compliance app has not worked for a week, and Ross has been nudged three times to help fix it.
Ross arranged for Peter Brown to do fire safety checks on Thursday although the next fire inspections are not due until November; Rory arrived at 8am to give access but no one turned up.
Glass washer issues are ongoing, and activating the warranty with Nisbets is proving difficult while the site waits for the sales order number from Junna before a visit can be arranged.
The sushi fridge could not be economically repaired, and the new one has arrived but removing the old one is a tricky job, with installation by Chris planned before service the next day.
A new induction hob was installed by Kris.
Five inside chairs are still missing and China stock is out of stock (Francheska), which reduces maximum covers and is hitting weekend sales.
New ramen allergen sheets still need printing because the ramen recipe has changed.
May and Tobi are on holiday until the end of the month, and Dylan is back from holiday.
The new KP, Ken, started last Thursday and is settling in well.
Nabina is covering sushi for three days next week.
A FOH team member will finish at the end of next week.

SPH (continued incentives to push sushi and sides) and cleanliness are the stated areas for improvement, and after the 05/10 roundtable a weekly bar checklist has been printed and put behind the bar and less frequent cleaning tasks are being tackled.
Asana tasks assigned by Michael are being worked through for the rest of the week.
Yan Ha will check storage space for the frozen ramen promotion, and Penny is concerned about space at the smaller sites and the unclear quantities per flavour.
XOXO and the Maki App are the upcoming promotions.

Region-wide (Scotland BOH meeting 06/10): last week's chicken broth usage discrepancy was traced to a takeaway recipe still linked to the old tonkotsu broth in stock counts, which has been corrected, so usage should return to normal next week.

Region-wide (Scotland BOH meeting 06/10): Bidfood is being brought in as a new supplier, starting with Aberdeen and reaching the other sites within one to two months, and new beef samples are being trialled with a view to pre-cooked beef so sites no longer cook it themselves.
